label: German Black Pied Dairy

names.text: The German name Schwarzbuntes Milchrind and the abbreviation SMR come from the WebSearch result text summarising the Wikipedia page, not the opened page. Schwarzbunte is the item's given name. Not to be confused with the German Black Pied (DSN), the older base population.

about.text: The German Black Pied Dairy was a dairy breed of former East Germany, made from 1963 by crossing Danish Jersey, German Black Pied and Holstein cattle. It was bred for high milk and milk fat yields with adequate beef performance. After German reunification it was largely displaced by the Holstein.

sources.text: All from the opened Wikipedia page: the 1963 proposal by Georg Schönmuth, the three-breed cross, the aim of high milk and fat with sufficient beef performance, and the displacement by Holsteins after reunification. The page describes it in the past tense.
From the opened Wikipedia page: the crossing was proposed in 1963 and the interse breeding continued until 1990.
The Wikipedia page calls it a dairy cattle breed. It aimed at high milk production and fat content, with sufficient beef performance as a secondary goal.

gaps: No milk yield, milk composition, population or head count was found on the opened Wikipedia page. No DAD-IS risk status was found and the page does not state whether the breed is extinct. The German-name aka comes only from search text. No other pages were opened for this breed within the search budget.
